comments: I tried to investigate on my mac (the test fails 30-50% of the runs), but I haven't found anything interesting. I suspect it's a bug in Node.js (not in the test), but I may be wrong.

> I tried to investigate on my mac (the test fails 30-50% of the runs), but I haven't found anything interesting. I suspect it's a bug in Node.js (not in the test), but I may be wrong.

This may be asking a lot but if you go to the commit where the test was first added, is it flaky there? If not, perhaps a (no doubt time-consuming) bisect might find something interesting?

> > I tried to investigate on my mac (the test fails 30-50% of the runs), but I haven't found anything interesting. I suspect it's a bug in Node.js (not in the test), but I may be wrong.
> 
> This may be asking a lot but if you go to the commit where the test was first added, is it flaky there? If not, perhaps a (no doubt time-consuming) bisect might find something interesting?

I'm afraid that's not possible because the test was added in 2018 and M1 mac support was added last year. IIRC, I've always seen it fail since I bought the laptop in January.

review_comments: I'm really confused by the fact that calling `stream.end()` after the `'end'` event is emitted on `stream` can have any effect.
`stream.end()` is the writable side, `'end'` is on the readable side. They are not directly related.
would it be possible to use `pipeline` somehow to simplify the test?

It would but it does not make much sense in my opinion. We can call `stream.respond()` and `stream.end()` when the destination stream emits `'finish'` and not use the `'end'` event but I would prefer to do it as soon as possible.
